pages.name: Overview
pages.html:
The sergeant at North Harbor told me the girl had no business asking the questions she asked. I asked him which questions. He did not care for that one either.

Jane Blackwell, Torch & Clarion

Held for Questioning

After the Skohle reading ends in murder, the Watch brings the survivors to North Harbor Police Headquarters to answer questions. Detective Hawkins wants to know what they saw in the dark. Down in the cells sits Benjamin Payne, bagman for Wystan Aldous of Brasshold. Merewyn Osgood means to answer Aldous in the only language he understands, and her gunmen are coming through a side door a bought sergeant left on the latch. In the morgue below lies the Smiling Man's latest victim, a bluestocking who asked too many questions. She will not stay on the slab.

Episode Summary
Players 3–6, Level 4
Duration ~4 hours
Pacing Interrogation; Combat; Escape
Scenes 6
Cast Detective Hawkins; Captain Till; Sergeant Knight; Benjamin Payne; Merewyn Osgood's gunmen; the Dancing Spinster
Reward The Murder Board; the station's papers; Brasshold's gratitude
References Doom Counter; Curse System; Dancing Spinster stat block; Police Headquarters and Morgue maps

Timeline

Four months ago. Dr. Aldous Pemberton attends a reading of a Pale Journal page above a tobacconist on Lantern Avenue. He is changed by it, and his shadow begins to hunt.

Two months ago. The first body is found in the lower wards, the skull opened above the eyebrows. The lower wards name the killer the Smiling Man.

Three days ago. Miss Prudence Quill, a bluestocking who had been asking questions above her station, is found dead in her rooms. She lies in the North Harbor morgue.

Last night. Sergeant Knight books Benjamin Payne into the cells on a minor charge, on Merewyn Osgood's coin.

Tonight. Claude Skohle's reading ends in murder. The Watch brings in everyone left standing.

Third bell. Merewyn's gunmen come through the side door.

Episode Structure

A police station under siege, then a morgue in the dark. The players are witnesses, not prisoners. Detective Hawkins questions them one at a time in front of his Murder Board, the station's whole case against the Smiling Man. What they read there carries them into Episode Two.

At the third bell, Merewyn Osgood's gunmen come through the side door to kill Payne and send Brasshold a message. The players fight them off, but fire and gunfire drive them down the stair into the morgue. There the Blue Stocking, Miss Quill, rises as the Dancing Spinster. She is far beyond a level four party. Getting out alive is the win.

pages.name: North Harbor Police Headquarters
pages.html:
Map Locations

1. Vestibule. Double doors to Harbor Street. A constable dozes on the bench by the door.

2. Duty Hall. Benches, pillars, and the sergeant's desk on its raised platform. Sergeant Knight keeps the blotter here.

3. Captain's Office. Parquet floor, a red desk, a wall safe. Captain Till keeps the door shut and the Osgood writ in his drawer.

4. Evidence Room. Shelves of tagged boxes and a locked wire cage. Payne's effects sit in the cage.

5. Detectives' Office. A rug, a long table, and the Murder Board on the wall. Hawkins questions the players here.

6. Muster Room. Benches where the constables take orders. Tonight the witnesses wait here.

7. Bunk Room. Cots for the night watch. Two constables sleep in their boots.

8. Armory. Racks of truncheons, service revolvers, a riot shotgun, and one Tommy gun in a locked case.

9. Storeroom. Crates of files and lamp oil. The side door opens onto the alley. Knight leaves it off the latch at the third bell.

10. Stair. Stone steps down to the morgue.

11. Turnkey's Desk. The cell log and the keys, at the head of the cell block.

12. Cell Block. Three corridors of barred cells. Payne is in the far corridor, alone.

Weapons

The players came as witnesses, so they keep what they carried in. When the shooting starts, the Armory (8) holds a riot shotgun, a Tommy gun, service revolvers and truncheons. The ammunition is in the Storeroom (9).

Doom

Mythos Disadvantage. Disadvantage on one roll: the hand shakes, the mind stalls.

Murphy's Law. A lamp tips, a key sticks, a cell door jams.

Everyone's a Suspect. Hawkins catches a player in a small lie and writes it down.

Lights Out, Somebody Screams. The gas fails on one room for a round.

Cut Off. A burning doorway or a jammed gate. The players must go around.

Enemy Reinforcements. One more gunman comes through the side door; below, the Spinster closes 10 feet.

Activate one Dread Ability. Trigger a Dread Insight already held by a player.

pages.name: The Morgue
pages.html:
Map Locations

13. Stair Hall. A long tiled hall from the foot of the stair. Cold enough to see breath.

14. Cold Room. Two walls of body drawers behind a heavy door. Packed earth beyond the walls.

15. Autopsy Room. Six slabs in two rows under hanging lamps. Miss Quill lies on the far slab under a sheet.

16. Coroner's Office. A lamp, a desk, the case files. The Coroner's Med Kit hangs by the door.

17. Laboratory. Benches, jars, a still, and a cabinet of instruments. Lamp oil, matches, and a cold-iron poker by the stove.

18. Specimen Store. Shelves of jars and a workbench. A dead end.

The Blue Stocking

Miss Prudence Quill read in the Meskawaki University library at night and asked the librarians about the Pale Journals. The Smiling Man took what she knew three days ago. Something of the shadow stayed in her. When the noise of the fight reaches the morgue, she gets up.

The Night at a Glance

Time What Happens (Scene)
1 AM The players arrive as witnesses (1)
1:30 AM Questioning at the Murder Board (2)
3 AM The third bell: the gunmen (3)
3:15 AM Fire and gunfire drive them below (4)
3:30 AM The Spinster wakes (5)
Dawn Aftermath (6)
Doom 6 The gunmen come at once (3)

Running the Questioning

Hawkins takes the players one at a time. While one is questioned, the others wait in the Muster Room (6) with a single constable. They can talk, listen at doors, and walk as far as the Duty Hall (2) before someone asks where they are going. Each player can attempt one bit of mischief while they wait: read the blotter, chat up the turnkey, look into the Evidence Room. Add 1 to the Doom Counter for each one that is noticed.

pages.name: Scene 1: Answering Questions
pages.html:
Duty Hall (2) and Muster Room (6), 1 AM. ~30 min

Gas lamps hiss above rows of oak benches. A sergeant's desk stands on a raised platform at the end of the hall, and beyond it a barred door leads to the cells.

What's Happening. The Watch has brought every survivor of the Skohle reading here as witnesses. No one is under arrest. Sergeant Dewey Knight takes their names at the desk and seats them in the Muster Room to wait for Detective Hawkins. Captain Till's door stays shut. Knight checks his watch against the hall clock more than a man on a quiet shift should.

Clues. The Blotter Page lies open on Knight's desk. A DC 13 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) or Charisma (Deception) check gets a look at it. Read against the guests at the reading, it shows two names missing: Miss Constance Sharp and Sir Reginald Stowe. A DC 14 Wisdom (Insight) check on Knight: he is waiting for something, and it is not the end of his shift.

Scene Flow. Let the players settle, trade what they saw at the reading, and try their one bit of mischief (see Running the Questioning). Hawkins calls the first of them in after a few minutes. Run Scene 2.

pages.name: Scene 2: The Murder Board
pages.html:
Detectives' Office (5), 1:30 AM. ~45 min

Photographs, pins and red thread cover the wall behind a long table. Across the top, in heavy capitals: THE SMILING MAN MURDERS.

What's Happening. Hawkins questions each player about the reading: who stood where, what they saw when the lights went out, what they heard. He is honest and tired, and he believes the Skohle killing is the Smiling Man's work. He wants a description. He has never had a good one.

Clues. Give the players the Murder Board handout and let them look while Hawkins talks. A player who describes what they saw at the reading earns his trust; he then shows them the Case Notes on the Skull-Cuts and tells them the freshest victim, Miss Quill, is downstairs. A DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check on the board finds Dr. Pemberton's name on the suspect list, crossed out: asleep at home. The Memo: Keep It Quiet is spiked on his desk; Hawkins resents it and does not hide it. The Telegraph Flimsy sits under it.

Scene Flow. Hawkins asks each player the same question three ways. A player caught in a lie adds 1 to the Doom Counter. Keep the interviews short and rotate; the players not in the room are waiting in the Muster Room. When the last player has been questioned, or the Doom Counter reaches 6, run Scene 3.

pages.name: Scene 3: The Third Bell
pages.html:
Storeroom (9), Cell Block (12) and Duty Hall (2), 3 AM. ~45 min

Somewhere in the city a bell strikes three. A cold draft runs the length of the corridor from the back of the building.

What's Happening. Merewyn Osgood's gunmen come through the side door Knight left off the latch, one gunman for each player, less one. They are here to kill Benjamin Payne in his cell and leave him for Wystan Aldous to find. They will shoot anyone between them and the cells. The constables fall back. Hawkins fights. Till locks his door. Knight "tries to help," and pulls a bystander in front of every shot aimed at him.

Clues. The Crumpled Note is in Knight's pocket. The Torn Ledger Page is in his desk. The Cell Log Slip at the Turnkey's Desk (11) shows Knight booked Payne himself. The Sealed Osgood Writ is in Till's drawer, unsigned.

Scene Flow. Payne, if freed, runs or bargains. If the players save him, Brasshold owes them. Run Scene 4 when the gunmen bring out the fire.

pages.name: Scene 4: Pushed Down
pages.html:
Stair (10) to Stair Hall (13), 3:15 AM. ~10 min

Burning lamp oil spreads across the flagstones. Smoke rolls along the ceiling toward the stair.

What's Happening. The gunmen cannot reach Payne quickly, so they burn their way in. A Molotov lays a wall of fire across the Duty Hall (2) and a grenade brings down the cell-block door. The way to the street is fire; the open way is the Stair (10). Payne bolts down it. Hawkins, wounded, goes after him.

Scene Flow. Drive the players down, do not drag them. Use the fire, Burst Fire into the hall, and the people they want to protect going below. If the players defeat the gunmen before the fire, the Associate Coroner screams from the morgue (Doom 9) and Hawkins goes down to look. Either way the players end up at the foot of the stair. Run Scene 5.

Hawkins's Questions

He asks An honest answer gives
Who brought you to the reading? He checks it against the blotter.
Where were you when the lights went out? Who stood nearest Skohle.
What did you see in the dark? His trust, and the Case Notes.
Did anyone leave the room? Sharp and Stowe are missing.
What is a Pale Journal page? He writes the words down.
Do you know a Dr. Pemberton? "Asleep at home. Crossed off."

pages.name: Scene 5: The Dance
pages.html:
Autopsy Room (15) and the morgue, 3:30 AM. Combat

Six stone slabs stand in two rows under hanging lamps. On the far slab a sheet lies on the floor.

What's Happening. Miss Quill is standing. Her neck has drawn out into a long pale lash with nothing at the end of it, and she is dancing. The Dancing Spinster acts after every player's turn. She walks walls and ceilings and never falls.

Clues. The Coroner's File on Miss Quill is in the Coroner's Office (16). The Coroner's Med Kit there can treat the Enfeebling Nox her Sapping Jig leaves. In the Laboratory (17): lamp oil, matches, and a cold-iron poker.

Scene Flow. This is not a fight to win. The Spinster moves only 10 feet at a time; players who run can outpace her on the floor, but not on the walls. Reward the players who get the wounded up the stair, set the morgue alight, or slam the Cold Room door between her and them. The scene ends when the players are out of the building or she is down.

pages.name: Scene 6: Aftermath
pages.html:
North Harbor Police Headquarters, dawn. ~15 min

What's Happening. The fire brigade puts out the Duty Hall. Captain Till takes charge, sends the witnesses home, and tells them they saw an Osgood raid and nothing else. The Spinster is gone if the players did not destroy her.

Clues. The Evidence Tag points to Payne's effects in the cage in the Evidence Room (4): an envelope of Brasshold money and a plain calling card. Anything the players picked up tonight goes home with them unless they are careless.

pages.name: Resolution
pages.html:
Outcome Ladder.

  • Total success. The players survive the Spinster, save Payne and Hawkins, and leave with the Murder Board read and the station's papers in their pockets.
  • Mixed. The players get out, but Payne or Hawkins dies, or the papers burn.
  • Total failure. The players flee with nothing but what they remember of the Murder Board.

Rewards. What they read on the Murder Board. Any papers they carried out. Wystan Aldous's gratitude if Payne lives. Hawkins's trust if he does.

Insight Cue. The Dancing Spinster is a Mythos exposure. Use the Spinster's Insight in the Bestiary.

Foreshadowing. The Telegraph Flimsy reports a man of science gone missing; it is a thread for later. Sharp and Stowe, missing from the blotter, are leads in Episode Two.

Threads and Dead Ends.

  • The Murder Board. The live thread. Pemberton's name is on it, crossed out.
  • Miss Quill. What she asked the librarians, and who answered.
  • The Osgood war. Merewyn hit Brasshold tonight. Aldous will answer.
  • Sergeant Knight. Bought. If the players expose him, Till buries it.
  • The Memo. "The Commander" is not Till. No one here will say who.

pages.name: Reading the Board
pages.html:
The victims. Professor Lydia Harrow (language), Dr. Emil Vey (the stars), Margaret Sloane (an artifact), Reverend Alistair Crowe (the rites). Each studied one piece of the same mystery.

The method. No tool marks. Each skull separated along its seams. Different parts of the brain taken from each, matching what each victim knew.

The witnesses. A flat black figure with a white smile and tears. It folds under doors and climbs walls.

The timeline. Every killing between 1:40 and 3:15 in the morning, while the city sleeps.

The suspects. A list of physicians, all crossed out. Dr. Pemberton among them: asleep at home, confirmed by his servant.

What the police missed. It wants what the victims remembered, not what they wrote. It moves through connected shadow and avoids strong light. Every murder happened while Pemberton slept.

For the DM. Let the players reach these conclusions themselves. Hawkins believes the Surgeon Theory.

pages.name: Running the Fight
pages.html:
The Gunmen

One gunman for each player, less one. Each turn a gunman fires the Tommy gun twice, or sprays a 10-foot cube with Burst Fire (DC 15 Dexterity), or throws a Molotov (a 15-foot wall of fire) or a grenade. They came for Payne. Players standing between the gunmen and Cell 9 draw the fire. When Payne is dead or out of reach, the survivors fall back through the side door.

The Constables

Two awake, two asleep in the Bunk Room (7). They Hit the Deck and Fall Back; they hold doors, they do not charge guns. Hawkins fights from cover with his snub revolver. Knight uses Grab a Bystander on anyone near him.

The Spinster

She takes one action after each player's turn and only moves on her own. Every action moves her 10 feet at most, across floors, walls and ceilings alike. Sapping Jig leaves an Enfeebling Nox; the Coroner's Med Kit (16) treats it. Drink Deep heals her by half the damage it deals, so a player she has coiled is a player to rescue first.

Ways Out

The Stair (10) is the only way up. The Cold Room (14) has a heavy door. Lamp oil from the Laboratory (17) burns.

pages.name: Cast
pages.html:
Detective Hawkins

North Harbor detective, forties.

AC18; HP51; Snub Revolver+7/2d8; Insight+2, Intimidation+2, Investigation+2

Description: Rumpled coat, loosened tie, a notebook gone soft at the corners.

Mannerisms: Asks the same question three ways. Writes down the answer that changes.

Intent: Wants a description of the Smiling Man. Honest, tired, and angry about the memo.

Captain Leonard Till

Station commander, fifties.

AC19; HP71; Officer's Revolver+9/2d8+2; Deception+3, Insight+3, Intimidation+3

Description: Pressed uniform, grey moustache, a desk with nothing on it.

Mannerisms: Answers questions with orders.

Intent: Follows the memo from above. Sat on Merewyn Osgood's writ rather than sign it. Locks his door when the shooting starts.

Sergeant Dewey Knight

Night sergeant, thirties.

AC18; HP34; Truncheon+7/1d8+2, Revolver+8/2d8+3; Deception+2, Intimidation+2

Description: Big, clean-shaven, a new watch on an old chain.

Mannerisms: Checks the time. Volunteers for the back corridor.

Intent: On Merewyn Osgood's payroll. Booked Payne, unlatched the side door, and stays out of the way.

Benjamin Payne

Bagman for Brasshold, in Cell 9.

AC16; HP10; Sap+3/1d4, Pistol+4/1d8; Deception+2, Sleight of Hand+2

Description: Good suit, bad shoes, a coin walking across his knuckles.

Mannerisms: Friendly to everyone. Knows the hour without a clock.

Intent: Carries Wystan Aldous's money. Will trade a word for a favor, and run the moment the door opens.

Associate Coroner

Night duty, the morgue.

AC15; HP5; Formalin+1/1d10+1; Medicine+2, Investigation+2

Intent: Wrote Miss Quill's file. Knows the body is wrong and says so to anyone who will listen.

Constables

The night watch.

AC16; HP10; Truncheon+3/1d4, Revolver+4/1d8; Perception+2

Intent: Duck, fall back, and follow Hawkins.

Osgood Gunmen

Merewyn Osgood's crew.

AC15; HP45; Tommy Gun x2 +5/2d8+3; Burst Fire, Molotov, Grenade

Intent: Kill Payne and leave him for Aldous to find. Shoot anything between them and the cells.

Author's Note

The players arrive as witnesses and leave as survivors. Let Hawkins push, let the Murder Board do its work, and do not hurry the third bell. The Spinster is far beyond a level four party. Getting out alive is a win. The Murder Board is what they carry into Episode Two.

pages.name: Horrors
pages.html:
The Dancing Spinster

Miss Prudence Quill. Mythos creature; see Bestiary.

AC21; HP286; Speed 10, climb 10; Whipping Neck+11/3d8+6, Drink Deep+12/6d8+11 necrotic; Legendary Resistance 3/day

Description: Blouse, corset and long dark skirt. Her neck drawn out into a pale lash with nothing at the end of it.

Mannerisms: Dances. Walks the walls and ceiling as easily as the floor.

Intent: Climbs toward noise and feeds on what it finds.

pages.name: Overview
pages.html:
The house on the hill has kept its lamps dark for a week. The milk is not taken in. The dog that barked at the gate has stopped barking, and nobody I asked could tell me when.

V.C. Lenore, Torch & Clarion

A Father's Bargain

Colonel Leopold Haeint, a retired army surgeon, could not save his dying daughter Anabelle. He had a mummy smuggled out of occupied Sai Abbadon, a war-priest of the Temple of Anhur set to guard the god's dead, and cut it apart in his tower laboratory to steal its deathless principle. Anabelle died anyway, but she did not leave: her spirit is held in a tank of alchemical fluid. The mummy woke, killed the Colonel and his wife, laid them out on slabs, and took up its post over the child. Now the Clarion Society wants to know why the Colonel has gone silent.

Episode Summary
Players 3–6, Level 5
Duration ~4 hours
Pacing Exploration; Investigation; Set-Piece
Scenes 6
Cast Bryony Thatch; Anabelle Haeint; the ghosts of Dr. and Mrs. Haeint; the Sentinel of Anhur
Reward A page of the Pale Journals; Curse Transfer
References Doom Counter; Curse System; Sentinel of Anhur stat block; Haeint House maps

Timeline

Fifteen years ago. A collector had the Pale Journals stolen from the Temple of Anhur in Sai Abbadon and brought to Anchester.

Two years ago. Zeshagu and Sous Terreborgue took Sai Abbadon. A year later their dragons and warships put Anchester under siege.

This spring. Anabelle Haeint falls ill with a wasting sickness. Every physician in the city gives up on her.

Weeks ago. Colonel Haeint obtains a page of the Pale Journals and has the Sentinel smuggled out of Sai Abbadon.

Days ago. Anabelle dies in the tank and lingers. The Sentinel wakes, kills the Colonel and his wife, and darkens the house.

Today. Bryony Thatch asks the players to find out why the Colonel has gone silent.

Episode Structure

A dark house and the truth inside it. The players come looking for a missing man and find a house with every lamp smashed. The house is the episode: they search it room by room, and the clues turn the story from "a monster killed everyone" into "the monster is guarding the child."

At the top of the house they find Anabelle in her tank, able to speak while the fluid holds her. The ghosts of her parents can be called to testify. The Sentinel of Anhur walks the house and senses every living thing in it.

There are two ways to end it. The players can light the tower and destroy the Sentinel, a brutal fight. Or they can help Anabelle finish crossing over. With its charge gone, the guardian stands down. The Pale Journal page in the Colonel's safe tells them which is right.

pages.name: The Haeint House: Ground Floor and Cellar
pages.html:
Map Locations

1. Front Porch. A deep veranda on three sides. The front door is unlocked. No one answers.

2. Center Hall. A long runner from the front door to the back. Every lamp on the walls is smashed. Drag marks lead up the Main Stair.

3. Parlor. Sofas around a cold fireplace. A family photograph on the mantel.

4. Music Room. A grand piano, lid open, sheet music on the floor.

5. Washroom. A small tiled room. The gas tap is wrenched shut.

6. Billiard Room. Cue rack, card table, a hide rug. The Colonel's brandy, untouched.

7. Dining Room. The table is set for three. The food has gone to mold.

8. Butler's Pantry. Silver, linen, and the household's spare lamps, every one broken.

9. Main Stair. Scorch marks and a spent lamp on the landing, where the Colonel drove it back with fire.

10. Back Stair. The cellar door and the stair down.

11. Back Porch. The kitchen garden and the gate to the lane.

12. Cellar. Wine racks, barrels, and stacked shipping crates stenciled with temple sigils.

Lighting the House

The Sentinel smashed or doused every flame and shut off the gas. The house is dark except for what the players carry. Bright light is the one thing that hurts it: track every light source the players bring in.

pages.name: The Second Floor
pages.html:
Map Locations

13. Upper Hall. A red-carpeted gallery around the stairwell. A spiral stair climbs to the attic.

14. Colonel's Study. Desk, globe, a wall of books. The safe behind the map case holds the Pale Journal page. The combination is the date of Anabelle's birth, written in the family Bible in the Parlor (3).

15. Anabelle's Room. A small bed under a round blue rug. Medicine bottles on every surface.

16. Master Bedroom. A great bed before the fireplace. Mrs. Haeint's diary is in the bedside table.

17. Guest Room. Dust sheets over the furniture.

18. Guest Room. Made up for a nurse who never came.

19. Spare Room. A narrow bed, trunks, and a dressmaker's form.

20. Bath. A claw-footed tub. The mirror is cracked from the inside out.

pages.name: The Attic and the Tower
pages.html:
Map Locations

21. Attic Hall. A long storeroom under the roof: crates, a carpet roll, an old field cannon from the Colonel's regiment.

22. West Attic. Benches and tool chests. The Colonel's warding kit. A spiral stair climbs to the tower.

23. Slab Room. Three stone slabs under the east eaves. Dr. and Mrs. Haeint lie on two of them, washed and laid out with care. The third is the dissection slab where the Sentinel lay, with snapped restraints and scattered chalk.

24. Tower Laboratory. The one room in the house with power. A humming tank of electrical and alchemical fluid stands against the wall. Anabelle floats inside.

Running the House

The Sentinel's post is the Tower Laboratory (24). Until the Doom Counter reaches 6 it stays there, and the players can search the lower floors freely, with only the dark and the drag marks for company.

It senses every living creature within 120 feet through walls and darkness. The players cannot hide from it, but it does not come for them unless they reach for the tank, or the Doom Counter says otherwise.

pages.name: Scene 1: The Dark House
pages.html:
Front Porch (1), dusk. ~15 min

A three-storey house stands at the end of the lane behind an iron gate. Every window is dark, and a narrow tower rises from the roof.

What's Happening. Colonel Leopold Haeint, a retired army surgeon and friend of Major Lyle Wakes, has stopped answering letters. Wakes is in hospital and Erasmus Byrgenwright will not leave his research, so Bryony Thatch, the youngest member of the Clarion Society, asks the players to look in on him. No one answers the door. It is not locked.

Clues. Bryony has the Colonel's last letter to Wakes (Clue 29): he writes that he has "found a way" and asks Wakes to come see. She knows the household is only the Colonel, his wife, and their sick daughter.

Scene Flow. Bryony comes along if the players let her. She is brave and useless in a fight. Run Scene 2 when the players step inside.

pages.name: Scene 2: Searching the House
pages.html:
The whole house, evening. ~90 min

The hall smells of lamp oil and something older, like dust from a sealed room. Glass crunches underfoot.

What's Happening. The house is dark and silent. The Sentinel is in the tower and knows the players are here. Let them search room by room using Map Locations and Found in the House.

Clues. Each room lists its clues. Reveal a clue when a player searches the right room; a DC 12 Intelligence (Investigation) check finds the smaller ones. The safe in the Study (14) needs the combination from the family Bible (3) or a DC 18 Dexterity check with thieves' tools.

Scene Flow. Add 1 to the Doom Counter for each hour of searching and for every loud noise. When the players have the story's broad shape, run Scene 3.

pages.name: Scene 3: Piecing It Together
pages.html:
Anywhere, as the clues come together. ~20 min

What's Happening. This is the turn of the episode. The early clues read like a massacre: smashed lamps, drag marks, a missing family. The later ones show a guardian: it carried the dead upstairs and laid them out, it stood watch over the tank, it did not harm the girl.

Clues. The turning point is any of Clues 16, 17 or 18. The resolution is in the Pale Journal page (the handout), which says the crossed-over can only be released, never revived.

Scene Flow. Ask the players what they think happened before they climb to the attic. Their answer decides how they walk into Scene 4.

Doom

Mythos Disadvantage. Disadvantage on one roll: the hand shakes, the mind stalls.

Murphy's Law. A match will not strike, a floorboard cracks, a door sticks.

Lights Out, Somebody Screams. One carried light goes out. The Sentinel knows where everyone is; the players do not.

A Door, My Old Nemesis. A door the players need is jammed or locked.

Cut Off. The Sentinel stands between the players and the stair.

From the Shadows. The Sentinel makes one Rotting Fist attack against a player in dim light or darkness, then withdraws.

Activate one Dread Ability. Trigger a Dread Insight already held by a player.

pages.name: Scene 4: Anabelle
pages.html:
Tower Laboratory (24). ~20 min

A tall glass tank stands in a frame of brass and wire, humming. A thin girl floats inside, eyes open, hair drifting in the green fluid.

What's Happening. Anabelle Haeint died in the tank and did not leave. While the fluid holds her she can speak, faintly, through the glass. If she is lifted out she dissolves into sludge and is gone. The Sentinel stands in the corner and does not move unless someone reaches for the tank.

Clues. Anabelle remembers the pain stopping, her father weeping, and "the tall man in the wrappings" who sends everyone away. She asks for her mother. She is tired. She wants to go to sleep and cannot.

Scene Flow. Any player who touches the tank, the valves, or the girl draws the Sentinel at once (Scene 6, The Fight). A player who talks to her can ask what she wants. Her answer is the Mercy.

pages.name: Scene 5: The Ghosts
pages.html:
Slab Room (23), or anywhere in the house. ~20 min

What's Happening. Dr. and Mrs. Haeint can be called back as ghosts to testify: by a ritual from the Colonel's notes, by a cleric's magic, or by speaking to them at their slabs. They are confused and grieving, and each holds half the story.

Clues. The Colonel confesses the smuggling, the page, and the experiments, and admits he cannot let her go. Mrs. Haeint saw the Sentinel kneel by the tank. She begs the players to let her daughter rest.

Scene Flow. The Colonel resists the Mercy. If the players move to release Anabelle, he possesses one of them (DC 13 Charisma) to stop it. Mrs. Haeint helps.

pages.name: Scene 6: Resolution
pages.html:
Tower Laboratory (24). Set-piece

The Fight. The players light the tower and destroy the Sentinel. In darkness it resists everything but fire and radiant damage and attacks with advantage. Bright light strips that away. Use Running the Sentinel. When it falls it stays down.

The Mercy. The players help Anabelle finish crossing over: by her mother's voice, by a prayer, or by draining the tank at her request, not against her will. As she goes, the Sentinel kneels. With its charge gone, it crumbles to dust and sand.

Either Way. The house is quiet. The page is theirs.

pages.name: Resolution
pages.html:
Outcome Ladder.

  • Total success. The players release Anabelle with her parents' blessing. The Sentinel stands down. They leave with the page and the whole story.
  • Mixed. The players destroy the Sentinel by fire and light. Anabelle is released or lost in the fight. They leave with the page.
  • Total failure. The players flee the house with the Rotting Hex in their blood and the page left behind.
  • Pyrrhic. The players lift Anabelle out to "save" her. She dissolves. The Sentinel fights to the end.

Rewards. The page of the Pale Journals, "Of the Borrowed Spark." Studying it teaches Curse Transfer and the formula for the Revitalizing Tincture.

Insight Cue. The Sentinel is a Mythos exposure. The first player to study the page loses 1d6 Sanity or makes a Wisdom save against short-term madness.

Foreshadowing. Days later, Colonel Standard of the Special Police seizes the Colonel's experiments and every note left in the house. The serum begins here.

Threads and Dead Ends.

  • The page. The live thread. It is the second page the players have seen.
  • The smuggler. Shipping papers name a fast boat out of Sai Abbadon.
  • Colonel Standard. He knew about the tank before the players did.
  • Major Wakes. He will want to know what became of his friend.

The Night at a Glance

Time What Happens (Scene)
Dusk The players arrive (1)
Evening Searching the house (2, 3)
Any time The tower: Anabelle (4)
After the slabs The ghosts (5)
Doom 12 The Sentinel hunts (6)

pages.name: Running the Sentinel
pages.html:
Umbral Fortitude

In dim light or darkness the Sentinel resists all damage except fire and radiant, attacks with advantage, and its Dreadful Glare and Blasphemous Word rise to DC 18. In bright light it loses the resistance, attacks with disadvantage, and its Rotting Fist deals no necrotic damage. Until the room is lit, treat it as having about 600 hit points.

Life-Sense

It knows where every living creature within 120 feet is, through walls and darkness, and which of them has the fewest hit points. Only a warded threshold, three feet of stone, or a sheet of lead blocks it. Anabelle does not register. The Lead-Foil Ward Charm, Warding Salt and Grave-Dust Sachet hide a player from it.

Guttering Gloom

A legendary action dims every ordinary light within 30 feet one step. The Oil of Quenchless Flame and the Magnesium Flare are the answers.

The Rotting Hex

Its Glare and its Blasphemous Word lay a Hex on Constitution. Each further failure while cursed climbs one tier: Hex, Nox, Pox, Curse, Damnation. Only once per turn on the same creature. Its Rotting Fist also carries mummy rot (DC 16 Constitution).

Tactics

It is a guardian, not a hunter. It wants the living away from Anabelle. It keeps the tower dark with Guttering Gloom and darkness, and uses Whirlwind of Dust to slip past the front line back to the tank. Anyone reaching for the tank is its first target.

Tuning for Level 5

As written it is deadly. Treat it as a set piece: the win is light and mercy, not damage. To soften it, drop its hit points to about 200 and its Legendary Resistance to 2/day, but keep Umbral Fortitude. Fire and radiant damage cut through even in darkness.

The Players' Dilemma

They must light the room to hurt it, while keeping it off the one spirit it exists to protect. Every round spent fighting near the tank is a round the tank can break. The wiser path is to stop endangering Anabelle and help her go.

The Revitalizing Tincture

With the page and a short rest at an alchemist's bench, a player can brew a draught that pulls a creature back from death's edge: stabilize and heal substantially, or lift one tier of a wasting curse or disease. The decay must go somewhere. The brewer chooses a vessel, a willing ally, an enemy, or themselves, and that vessel takes a Rotting Hex of the same tier.

Curse Transfer

Studying the page teaches Curse Transfer: push a weaker curse onto another creature and promote your own one tier. The page names it the true mechanism of revitalization: you do not heal the rot, you move it.

Author's Note

This is a haunted house with a grieving monster in it. Let the players search, let the clues turn the story, and let them decide what kind of people they are at the top of the stairs. The fight is the brute-force answer. The Mercy is the right one, and the page tells them so.

MRS. HAEINT'S DIARY

It killed him. I saw it. And then it went to her tank and knelt, like a soldier at a grave, and it has not moved since. It is not a monster. It is a sentry. God help me, it is guarding my girl.

Such guardians cannot be commanded, bought, or bound. They ward their charge. Remove the charge and you remove the reason. Threaten it and you will learn what the temple paid for.

Lyle. I have found a way. It is not medicine and it is not God, but it is a way. Come and see her. Come soon. Burn this.

L.H.

pages.name: Overview
pages.html:
The Killing Ground

The evidence and the changed men shipped north ahead of the party, into the Battle of Paschendale. The serum turned the volunteers into jackal-headed warriors, and every early sign called the project a success. Then they tasted blood. They went berserk. They killed the enemy, their allies, and one another. Only one soldier kept his mind, Sergeant Freitman Bay. The rumor on the field is that the Special Police took him away in chains, in the armored coach that carried off Colonel Standard and Dr. Pemberton. The man in chains was Corporal Aberdeen. Bay slipped them and fled south into the wilderness after his bride, and now everyone is hunting him. The party arrives to a handful of shell-shocked regulars and a field full of the dead.

Episode Summary
Players 3–6, Level 8
Duration ~4 hours
Pacing Hex Crawl; Exploration; Combat
Scenes 4
Cast Shell-shocked regulars; a Sister of Mercy; a Sous Terreborgue prisoner; six horrors of the field
Reward A page of the Pale Journals, if the map case turns up; the trail south
References Doom Counter; Curse System; E04 Bestiary; Hex Table; Paschendale map; battlefield maps

Timeline

Fifteen years ago. A collector had the Pale Journals stolen from the Temple of Anhur in Sai Abbadon.

Two years ago. Zeshagu warriors joined Sous Terreborgue and took Sai Abbadon.

One year ago. Zeshagu's dragons and Sous Terreborgue's warships sealed Anchester. The collector had the Journals copied, and pages leaked into the city.

Six months ago. The Special Police secretly began building super-soldiers from something found in one of the stolen Journals.

Three months ago. Academics were found dead, skulls opened above the brow. The wards named the killer the Smiling Man.

These past weeks. The players hunted the Smiling Man to the Garrison and seized the evidence the Special Police were shipping north.

Yesterday. At Paschendale the serum turned the volunteers, and they slaughtered the enemy, their allies, and one another.

Today. The players reach the battlefield to take up the trail.

Episode Structure

A hex crawl across the drowned battlefield. The players arrive at the Anchester line, hear the rumor of the coach, and go out onto the field to find what is left of the volunteers.

Each hex is 100 yards across. When the party enters a hex, roll on the Hex Table for what is there: the dead, the living, salvage, wreckage, ground, the Abhorrent, clues, or quiet dread. About one hex in seven holds one of the six horrors, the two Epic Bosses included, and about one in six holds nothing. Everything on the table is random, the Pale Journal page and the leads to Bay included.

The DM can put a finger on the scale: place any find or horror instead of rolling for it.

The episode ends when the party leaves the field with what it found, or when the field drives them off.

Start: equal to the party's number of Dread Insights.

Add 1 Doom for every three hexes crossed, for every gunshot or flare, and the first time blood is spilled in a hex.

Escalating Doom

Mark Escalation
3 Fog. The party sees only the hex it is in.
6 Each hex also holds a horror on a d6 roll of 1 or 2.
9 Rain floods the craters. All standing water holds Unholy Mackerel.
12 The Gallows hunts the party and enters their next hex.

Manifesting Doom

Cost Doom
1 Mythos Disadvantage
1 Murphy's Law
2 The Duckboards Give Way
2 Cut Off

5 Activate one Dread Ability

pages.name: Paschendale
pages.html:
Reading the Map

Each hex is 100 yards across. The sea and the sandbars lie to the northwest; Sous Terreborgue wants the long beach for a landing, and the Anchester Army dug in to stop it. Wooded high ground rings the field. Everything between is marsh, flooded craters, and channels, with duckboard tracks the only dry way across.

Moving on the Field

Off the duckboards, a hex takes twice as long to cross, and a character who leaves the track in standing water risks the Unholy Mackerel once the Doom Counter reaches 9. Woods on the high ground give cover and slow the horrors that drag themselves.

Fights on the Field

When a horror turns up, run the fight on one of the six battlefield maps in Foundry (04.03.01 to 04.03.06). Pick the one whose craters and trenches suit the hex.

Doom

Mythos Disadvantage. Disadvantage on one roll.

Murphy's Law. A rifle jams, a flare fails, a boot sticks fast.

The Duckboards Give Way. A player drops into a flooded crater, prone in water to the chest.

Cut Off. Wire or water blocks the way forward; the party must go around.

The Dead Rise. A Grafted Reservist stands up from the nearest corpse.

Activate one Dread Ability. Trigger a Dread Insight already held by a player.

pages.name: Scene 1: The Line
pages.html:
The Anchester line, south of the field. Grey dawn. ~20 min

A trench line runs along the ridge above the field. Below it, the ground is water and mud as far as the fog allows.

What's Happening. A handful of shell-shocked regulars hold the line. Their officers are dead or gone. The Special Police left yesterday in an armored coach, with Colonel Standard and Dr. Pemberton inside.

Clues. Any regular will tell the party the rumor: the Special Police took the one sane survivor away in chains. They will point the coach's road north and back toward the city. None of them went out onto the field after the volunteers turned, and none will go now.

Skill Checks

Insight DC 12. The regulars repeat what they were told, not what they saw.

Persuasion DC 14. A regular shows the party the duckboard track onto the field.

Scene Flow. When the party steps off the line, run Scene 2.

pages.name: Scene 2: The Field
pages.html:
Paschendale. Day. ~2 hours

What's Happening. The party crosses the field hex by hex. Roll on the Hex Table for every hex entered. Track the Doom Counter.

Clues. The finds under Clues and Leads (57 to 64) tell the true story: the coach doubled back south, the manacles were wrenched open, and bare footprints run south into the wilderness. The map case (30) holds a Pale Journal page.

Skill Checks

Survival DC 13. Each hex crossed off the duckboards. On a failure, add 1 Doom.

Investigation DC 15. On a Clues and Leads find. On a success, the party reads the true story in it: the ruts double back, the manacles were wrenched open.

Scene Flow. When the table turns up a horror, run Scene 3.

pages.name: Scene 3: The Abhorrent
pages.html:
Any hex. ~30 min each

What's Happening. One of the six horrors is in the hex. The Grafted Reservists come in numbers; the Questing Remnants come to blood; the Unholy Mackerel own the water. The Unholy Cow and The Gallows are Epic Bosses.

Clues. Every horror is a leaving of the serum. Abhorrent flesh outlives its host and reaches for a new one.

Scene Flow. Return to Scene 2. A party that runs may lose the horror only by leaving the hex.

pages.name: Scene 4: Leaving the Field
pages.html:
The edge of the field. ~15 min

What's Happening. The party leaves the field with whatever it found. If it found the footprints, the ring, or the letter, it knows Bay went south toward the city on foot. If not, it leaves believing the rumor of the chained man in the coach.

Skill Checks

Survival DC 15. With the footprints (58) found, the party follows them to the road south. Bay is on foot, headed for the city.

Scene Flow. Episode Five begins in Anchester, with Bay loose in the city.

pages.name: Resolution
pages.html:
Outcome Ladder.

  • Total success. The party finds the trail south and the page, and leaves before Doom 12.
  • Mixed. The party finds the trail or the page, not both.
  • Total failure. The party leaves believing the rumor, with nothing in hand.
  • Pyrrhic. The Gallows comes for them, and someone stays on the field.

Rewards. The Pale Journal page, if found. Salvage from the table: starmetal rounds, Halloran's Salts, Dr. Boonsboro's Nervine.

Insight Cue. The first player to look into the pit of failures (51) or face The Gallows makes a Wisdom save against short-term madness.

Foreshadowing. The armored coach is already back in Anchester, and so is the man in chains.

Threads and Dead Ends.

  • Sergeant Bay. Fled south. Episode Five.
  • Corporal Aberdeen. In the coach, in chains. The party does not know yet.
  • The Garrison Times. The city will hear Paschendale was a victory.

Running the Living

The living on the field (11 to 20) are the party's best source of the true story. Each knows one piece of it. Calm them, and they talk; frighten them, and they repeat the rumor.

Running the Dead

The Abhorrent flesh is a parasite. Any corpse the party passes may be what rises when the Doom Counter reaches The Dead Rise.

Not on the Field

Sergeant Freitman Bay. The one volunteer who kept his mind. Fled south on foot after his bride, Claudia. Episode Five.

Corporal Aberdeen. The man in chains in the coach. Embraced the serum and did the real killing. The party does not know.

Colonel Standard and Dr. Pemberton. Gone in the armored coach, back toward the city.

pages.name: Cast
pages.html:
Shell-Shocked Regular

Anchester infantry, any age.

AC12; HP22; Rifle+4/1d10+2; Bayonet+4/1d6+2

Field nurse, Church of the Martyr.

AC11; HP18; Scalpel+3/1d4+1; Medicine+6

Boy Soldier

Drummer, fifteen.

AC11; HP9; Knife+2/1d4

Description: Too small for the coat, eyes too old for the face.

Mannerisms: Starts every answer with "Sir."

Intent: Saw it all, the jackal heads, the coach, the chained man. Will tell it if calmed.

Sous Terreborgue Prisoner

Dwarven infantryman, captured.

AC14; HP26; Fists+3/1d4+2

Description: Heavy kit, steam-scald on one hand, bound at the wrists.

Mannerisms: Speaks Common badly and fast.

Intent: Saw the coach leave and the chained man break free. Wants to go home.

Half-Turned Man

Volunteer, failing.

AC13; HP40; Claw+6/2d6+3

Description: One hand gone to a claw, a muzzle pushing through the jaw.

Mannerisms: Lucid in short spells, then not.

Intent: Knows what he is becoming. Asks for mercy.

Deserter

Anchester infantry, hiding in a crater.

AC12; HP22; Rifle+4/1d10+2

Description: No cap, no badge, a rifle he keeps pointed at the party.

Mannerisms: Whispers. Watches the fog, not the party.

Intent: Thinks the party are Special Police come for him. Knows where the failures were dumped (51).

Blinded Gunner

Artillery, Anchester.

AC11; HP16; Pistol+3/1d8+1

Description: Bandage over both eyes, one hand on the duckboard rail.

Mannerisms: Turns his head toward sounds no one else hears.

Intent: Get back to the line. Heard the coach pull away, and which way it went.

pages.name: Horrors
pages.html:
Grafted Reservist

Medium undead, CR 5. Comes in numbers.

AC12; HP24; Speed 20; Grafted Strike+4/2d6+4; Reaching Blow+5/4d8+4 (rech 5); Grasping Reach DC12 Str

Description: A regular's corpse driven by a scrap of Abhorrent tissue grafted into it: the arm that swings too hard, the jaw that bites through bone, the rest of the body a moment behind.

Mannerisms: Lurches. Disadvantage on Dexterity saves. Undead Fortitude keeps it standing.

Intent: Spread. It attacks the nearest living thing and works its own loose flesh into the wound.

Traits. Undead Fortitude: at 0 HP, a Con save (DC 5 + damage) leaves it at 1 HP, unless the damage is radiant or a critical hit. Uncoordinated Frame: disadvantage on Dexterity saves.

Actions. Grafted Strike +4, 2d6+4 bludgeoning. Reaching Blow (recharge 5) +5, 4d8+4 bludgeoning, driving Abhorrent tissue into the wound. Grasping Reach (bonus action): DC 12 Strength or grappled; it holds one creature at a time.

Questing Remnant

Tiny aberration, CR 7. Answers blood.

AC15; HP94; Speed 10, climb 10, burrow 5; Climb On+6/4d6+3; Burrow In+7/6d8+7 and Rotting Pox (rech 5)

Description: A severed hand, a length of arm, a knot of muscle, crawling the mud for a body to take. Near invisible among the dead until it moves.

Mannerisms: Knows where anything wounded within 60 ft. is, and has advantage against it. Climbs onto its target; Dart Between and Skitter.

Intent: Get inside someone. Killing the corpse it came from does nothing; it left already.

Traits. Bloodscent: knows where every wounded creature within 60 ft. is. Answers Blood: advantage against a creature damaged this round. Barely There: in dim light, darkness, or still among the mud and dead, Perception to see it has disadvantage.

Actions. Climb On +6, 4d6+3 piercing; it climbs onto a Medium or smaller target. Burrow In (recharge 5) +7, 6d8+7 piercing and the Rotting Pox. Dart Between (bonus action): move 10 ft. through other creatures. Skitter (reaction): move 10 ft.

Unholy Mackerel

Medium swarm of Tiny aberrations, CR 6. Terrain hazard.

AC13; HP54; Speed 5, swim 60, fly 20 (hover); Boiling Teeth+11/6d6 and Grappled (DC14); Dragging Frenzy+12/12d6 (rech 5)

Description: A school of needle-toothed fish boiling in a flooded shell-hole, a few wearing the teeth and finger-bones of the men they stripped.

Mannerisms: Advantage against the wounded (Blood in the Water). Drags a victim 15 ft. and under; Whirlpool Wake pulls.

Intent: Strip whatever enters the water. On dry ground they flop and die. Keep to the duckboards.

Traits. Swarm: occupies a Medium space, moves through any opening a fish could; cannot regain HP or gain temporary HP. Blood in the Water: advantage against a creature at half HP or less, or damaged this round.

Actions. Boiling Teeth +11, 6d6 piercing, then DC 14 Strength or grappled. Dragging Frenzy (recharge 5) +12, 12d6 piercing and dragged 15 ft., under if the water is 5 ft. deep. Whirlpool Wake (bonus action): DC 14 Strength or pulled 10 ft. The Water Boils (reaction): moves toward a creature that takes damage.

Anubian Crawler

Medium aberration, CR 9.

AC19; HP240; Speed 20, climb 10; two attacks: Jackal Jaws+9/4d10+5; Throatstrike+10/8d10+10 (rech 5); Drag Down DC17

Description: A jackal-headed torso with no legs, hauling itself on ropes of its own abdominal muscle. The proportion study on the brass plate in the Garrison (Episode Three) was a drawing of this.

Mannerisms: Cannot be knocked prone. Resists non-silvered weapons. Flanks; Will Not Stop (DC15 Con to drop to 1 HP instead).

Intent: The throat. Of the crawling horrors it came closest to a finished super-soldier, and it fights like one.

Traits. Legless Speed: never slowed by prone, cannot be knocked prone. Serum-Wrought Flesh: resists non-silvered weapons. Fragment of Training: advantage against a target next to one of its allies. Multiattack: two attacks a turn.

Actions. Jackal Jaws +9, 4d10+5 piercing. Throatstrike (recharge 5) +10, 8d10+10 piercing; a critical hit on 15+ against a grappled target. Drag Down (bonus action): DC 17 Athletics or Acrobatics or grappled. Muscle-Rope Sprint (bonus action): 10 ft. Flanking Instinct and Will Not Stop (reactions).

Unholy Cow

Large aberration, CR 8 Epic Boss.

AC16; HP143; Speed 20; Charge and Gore+8/4d8+5; Trampling Charge+9/8d8+10 (rech 5); Rumen Vomit DC15 Con 3d6 poison and Rotting Pox (rech 4)

Description: A dairy cow that grazed where the serum-soaked dead lay. Bloated, hide split over grafted muscle, the bones of the men it swallowed pressing against its flank.

Mannerisms: From a distance, only a cow in the mist. Slow to rouse. Blood Grazing heals it 20 when it feeds on the fallen.

Intent: Charge, gore, trample, and then, slowly, eat. More of them low in the far pastures.

Epic Boss. It does not roll initiative. Each ability is a Response, used once per round after a player's action, then recharged. On its own turn it only moves.

Responses. Charge and Gore +8, 4d8+5 piercing. Trampling Charge (recharge 5) +9, 8d8+10 bludgeoning. Rumen Vomit (recharge 4) DC 15 Con, 3d6 poison and the Rotting Pox. Blood Grazing: moves 10 ft. to the fallen and regains 20 HP. Epic Boss Resistance: shakes off a condition on 11+.

The Gallows

Huge aberration, CR 12 Epic Boss.

AC21; HP330; Speed 15; Puppet Strike+14/6d10+4 (rech 2); Fling Puppet+15/12d10+8; Automatic Burst+14/6d10+4; Devouring Bite+15/16d8+16 (rech 5); Draining Snare+14/4d10+8

Description: Once an Anubian Crawler that did not stop feeding. A great jackal head on a mound of tentacles, each ending in a dead soldier worn like a glove.

Mannerisms: Corpse Curtain: ranged attacks against it have disadvantage. Uncoil Reserve replaces a lost puppet. Resists non-silvered weapons.

Intent: Harvest every fresh corpse. To end it, reach the head through the swinging dead.

Epic Boss. It does not roll initiative. Each ability is a Response, used once per round after a player's action, then recharged. On its own turn it only moves. Melee attackers within 10 ft. get past the Corpse Curtain.

Responses. Puppet Strike (recharge 2) +14, 6d10+4 slashing. Fling Puppet (recharge 5) +15, 12d10+8 bludgeoning, pushed 15 ft. Automatic Burst (recharge 4) +14, 6d10+4 piercing, 240 ft. Devouring Bite (recharge 5) +15, 16d8+16 piercing and grappled. Draining Snare (recharge 4) +14, 4d10+8 slashing; it regains 10 HP. Uncoil Reserve (recharge 3): a new puppet.

pages.name: Overview
pages.html:
The Missing Bride

Freitman Bay lived through the last episode, and his wife Claudia is still missing. She is on the run with her friend Evelyn Ridgely, carrying Bay's unborn child. The Special Police are hunting both women for the Clairvoyant, the hidden power the state answers to, and they are emptying the city of anyone who could help: Claudia's parents, a perfumer, a university professor. The papers call the vanished a Pixie Dust ring. The Smiling Man is killing again. The party follows the trail of the two women, and every lead runs toward the Special Police safehouses where Dr. Pemberton sleeps.

Episode Summary
Players 3–6, Level 10
Duration ~4 hours
Pacing Point-Crawl Investigation; Social; Combat
Scenes 14 locations and the safehouse
Cast The Ridgelys; Hamilton Frederick, PI; Hazel Attwater; Widow Ashe; the Special Police; the Smiling Man
Reward Dr. Pemberton, alive; Evelyn Ridgely; the safehouse journal
References Doom Counter; Dread Insight; Curse System; E06 stat blocks; safehouse map; eight broadsheets

Timeline

Fifteen years ago. A collector had the Pale Journals stolen from the Temple of Anhur in Sai Abbadon.

One year ago. Zeshagu's dragons and Sous Terreborgue's warships sealed Anchester. Pages of the Journals leaked into the city.

Six months ago. The Special Police began building super-soldiers from a serum found in one of the Journals.

Weeks ago. At Paschendale the serum turned the volunteers into monsters. The city was told it was a victory.

Days ago. Freitman Bay came home hunting his wife. The players saved him. Claudia and Evelyn were already in hiding.

Today. The Special Police are closing on the two women, and the Smiling Man has opened another skull.

Episode Structure

A manhunt with one goal: find Claudia. The players move freely across the wards. Each location holds a clue and points to one or two others. None of them leads straight to Claudia; the trail is bait, and every thread runs toward the people hunting her.

While the players search, the Special Police act offscreen, marked on the Doom Counter. When the Counter reaches 12, the finale happens at whichever safehouse the party is in or heading for. Claudia is already gone.

The two safehouses, Rue Blanc in Brasshold and Vine Street at Union Station, point to each other. When timing calls for it, skip the pointer and let the finale be at the safehouse the party has reached.

pages.name: The Doom Counter
pages.html:
Start: equal to the party's number of Dread Insights.

Add 1 Doom for every location visited, every fight, and every broadsheet that reaches the Special Police.

Escalating Doom

Mark Escalation
3 The Special Police take Claudia and Evelyn.
6 Standard takes Claudia to the Clairvoyant. Pemberton holds a safehouse.
9 The Smiling Man slips out to hunt. Hand out a Torch & Clarion.
12 The finale.

Manifesting Doom

Cost Doom
1 Mythos Disadvantage
1 Murphy's Law
2 Shut Door
2 Plain Clothes
3 Disappeared
5 Activate one Dread Ability

pages.name: Running the Crawl
pages.html:
Go % is the chance a party with no lead ends up there anyway; use it to judge which places the players will reach. Fight % is the chance a fight breaks out during the visit; roll once per visit, or decide.

Points To is a breadcrumb, never a route. Each lead names a place, and a ward to find it in. Getting closer is presentation: leads run warmer, the broadsheets darken, the Counter climbs.

The broadsheets. Each location has a paper lying about, pinned up, or pressed into the party's hands. Hand out the page when the players pick it up. Every paper hides one clue in a side column.

The Enemy Clock

The players never see the Special Police at work, only what they leave behind. At Doom 3 they take the two women from the Sheets. At Doom 6 the Clairvoyant summons Colonel Standard, and Standard leaves with Claudia, leaving Dr. Pemberton to hold the safehouse with a Captain and four Special Guards. At Doom 9, with Standard gone, Pemberton falls asleep and the Smiling Man goes hunting.

The Safehouse Chain

Both safehouses look abandoned until Doom 12. In each, the party finds Evelyn's handbag and the name of the other safehouse scratched into a doorframe. The Smiling Man's victims turn up near both.

If the Players Stall

Widow Ashe and Hamilton Frederick both point to Rue Blanc. Hazel Attwater points to both safehouses. Use them as the safety valve.

Fights in the City

Run fights on the location's map in Foundry (06.03 to 06.15). The Special Police come in squads: a Captain or two Special Guards per player. A Hungry Crowd fills any street in the poor wards. The Watch fights in uniform and gives up easily.

Running the Clairvoyant

The players learn that the Clairvoyant exists: the Special Police answer to it, and it wants Claudia's child. They learn nothing about who it is. No location, witness, or paper in this episode says more.

Doom

Mythos Disadvantage. Disadvantage on one roll.

Murphy's Law. A lamp gutters, a door sticks, a cab throws a wheel.

Shut Door. A witness has been warned off and will not talk without a DC 18 check.

Plain Clothes. Two Special Guards shadow the party to the next location.

Disappeared. A named witness the party has not yet met is taken. Their location is empty.

Activate one Dread Ability. Trigger a Dread Insight already held by a player.

pages.name: Ash Ward
pages.html:
The Easton House (Hamilton Row). Claudia's parents, Alfred and Maud Easton, butler and lady's maid to the Ridgelys. The door is broken and the house turned over. The neighbors watched the Special Police take the couple at night and say nothing unless pressed. On the floor: a photograph of Claudia and Evelyn, and a paycheck signed Ridgely.

Skill Checks

Investigation DC 12. The paycheck and the photograph name Evelyn and the Ridgelys.

Persuasion DC 14. A neighbor saw the wagon's markings: Special Police.

The Sheets. The shanty town of the poor. The two women hid here with Evelyn's friend Nancy Mallamore until the Special Police dragged them out. Bette Huerlock, a washerwoman, saw it and will tell it for a meal. A Hungry Crowd turns on anyone who looks like police.

Skill Checks

Persuasion DC 13. Bette describes the raid. The wagons were Union Station Watch, the men inside were not.

Intimidation DC 15. The crowd parts. On a failure, the Hungry Crowd attacks.

pages.name: East Row
pages.html:
Claudia's Perfume Shop. Shuttered, a Special Police notice on the door. Cissy Gelena sells flowers from a cart outside and liked Claudia. She saw police come asking for two girls and heard them say "the Sheets."

Widow Ashe. The fortune teller the Ridgelys hired. Every time she scries for the girls, something dark slams the door on her. She has seen one thing clearly: a yard of brass and soot, a white street sign, Rue Blanc. For a séance she can try again with the party at the table; it draws the Yfelgaest, a poltergeist that throws the parlour at them.

Skill Checks

Insight DC 14. Widow Ashe is frightened of what she saw, not of the party.

Arcana DC 16. The darkness that blocks her is a shadow with a will of its own.

pages.name: Meskawaki University
pages.html:
Evelyn's Dorm. Her roommate says Evelyn left to help Claudia hours before the police came, and names their friend Nancy Mallamore in the Sheets. Special Police watch the building.

Dr. Magrat's Office. Professor Magrat, Evelyn's supervisor, is gone. A note on his desk says the Special Police "engaged" him for an investigation.

Hazel Attwater. The underground journalist who prints The Worker. She hides her press in a cellar under the university and trusts no one sent by money. Win her over and she shows the report her source lifted from a Special Police courier, and gives the two addresses it names.

Skill Checks

Persuasion DC 16. Hazel trusts the party. On a failure, she gives them a copy of The Worker and shows them out.

Stealth DC 14. The party leaves the dorm without the watchers following.

pages.name: North Ward
pages.html:
The Special Police Garrison. The ward the Special Police took over for their own. Desk Sergeant Cecil Frost hides behind procedure and the ledger. Colonel Standard has not been seen here since Paschendale. In the cells: shopkeepers, the Eastons, and Professor Magrat. Getting in means a squad of Special Guards and a Captain.

Skill Checks

Deception DC 16. Frost lets the party read the ledger: the raid on the Sheets was signed out to the Union Station Watch House.

Stealth DC 15. The party reaches the cells unseen.

The Ridgely House (Brownstone Villas). Augustus and Georgiana Ridgely, rich and frantic, are paying for a private search. They will pay the party too. They name the two people they hired: Hamilton Frederick and Widow Ashe.

The Repose. The Coroner's Court. Assistant Coroner Aubrey Salisbury, a records man, is rattled: the skull-killings have started again, a body was found in the Meskawaki library, and the Special Police seize the bodies and close his inquests. His records show the newest bodies came from Brasshold, near Rue Blanc.

pages.name: North Harbor
pages.html: Hamilton Frederick, PI. A hard-bitten investigator working for the Ridgelys. He has three broadsheets pinned to his wall and a source who says Standard has gone rogue. He has an address in Brasshold: a Special Police safehouse on Rue Blanc.

pages.name: Union Station
pages.html:
The Watch House. The cabs and trolleys station's police post. Sergeant Henry Sharpe's men lent their wagons to the raid on the Sheets. Standard rode with them and took two women. The driver heard him say "Vine Street." The Watch fights if the party forces the door.

Skill Checks

Intimidation DC 14. Sharpe gives up the driver.

pages.name: The Safehouses
pages.html:
Rue Blanc, Brasshold and Vine Street, Union Station. Two requisitioned flats on ordinary terraced streets. Before Doom 12, each is empty: Evelyn's handbag under a bed, chains on a bedframe, and the name of the other safehouse scratched into the bedroom doorframe. At Doom 12, the one the party enters is the finale.

Roads Not Taken

Nancy Mallamore. Evelyn's friend in the Sheets. She hid the two women and saw them taken.

Freitman Bay. Alive and hunted as a witness. He is not in this episode.

pages.name: The Safehouse
pages.html:
Reading the Map

Both safehouses share this plan. The front steps open into the study. A hall runs from the study past the kitchen to the parlour and both bedrooms. Every room has shuttered windows. Map: 06.04 Rue Blanc or 06.11 Vine Street in Foundry.

1. Study. Desk, books, papers. One Special Guard. The journal is in the desk.

2. Hall. Runs the length of the flat.

3. Parlour. Three Special Guards at cards.

4. Kitchen. The Captain, at the table, with a view down the hall.

5. Back bedroom. Dr. Pemberton, asleep.

6. Front bedroom. Evelyn Ridgely, chained to the bed.

pages.name: The Finale: The Safehouse
pages.html:
Rue Blanc or Vine Street. Night. ~60 min

An ordinary terraced flat, shutters closed, a lamp lit in the kitchen. Behind one door, a man is snoring.

What's Happening. Claudia is gone; Standard took her to the Clairvoyant. Dr. Pemberton holds the flat with a Captain and four Special Guards, Evelyn chained in the front bedroom. Pemberton is asleep. His shadow is out hunting.

Getting In. The players choose: the front steps or any shuttered window. Do not fix a breach point.

Round 1. The Special Police fight. The Captain, in the kitchen, reinforces whichever end of the flat the players hit.

Round 2. The Smiling Man comes home. It appears in the back bedroom at the foot of Pemberton's bed, wherever the fight is.

Round 3. Pemberton wakes. The moment he is awake, the Smiling Man is pulled back into his shadow and trapped there. It cannot leave while he stays awake.

Clues. Players who read the Smiling Man's journal (Episode Five) know the shadow walks only while the doctor sleeps. Keeping Pemberton awake keeps it trapped.

Skill Checks

Athletics DC 15. Force the shutters. Daylight through a window puts the Smiling Man under Sundered by Sunlight.

Sleight of Hand DC 14. Pick Evelyn's chains, or take the key from the Captain.

Medicine DC 13. Keep Pemberton awake through the night: smelling salts, cold water, talk.

The Smiling Man. It is not beaten by damage. It leaves when Pemberton wakes, when daylight reaches it, or when it chooses Bag Trick.

pages.name: Resolution
pages.html:
Outcome Ladder.

  • Total success. Evelyn freed, Pemberton taken alive and kept awake, the journal in hand.
  • Mixed. Pemberton taken, Evelyn lost, or the reverse.
  • Total failure. The Smiling Man takes Pemberton with it into the bag. Evelyn is moved.
  • Pyrrhic. Pemberton is taken, and a player has been Excised.

Rewards. The journal from the study. Evelyn, who saw Standard leave with Claudia. Pemberton, a captive who must never sleep.

Insight Cue. Every player who sees the Smiling Man makes the Weeping Smile save; at the end of the fight, a Mythos Event save or a Dreadful Insight.

Foreshadowing. Evelyn heard Standard say he was taking Claudia to the Clairvoyant.

Threads and Dead Ends.

  • Claudia. In Standard's hands. Episode Seven.
  • Pemberton. No one stays awake forever.
  • The Clairvoyant. Real, and holding the Bride.

Keeping Him Awake

Pemberton is a man of AC 11 and 13 HP. He does not fight. He begs to sleep. Every night he is held, a player keeps watch.

pages.name: Cast
pages.html:
Augustus and Georgiana Ridgely

Old-money merchants, North Ward.

Description: Good clothes slept in. A drawing room full of telegrams.

Mannerisms: He offers money; she asks about Evelyn.

Intent: Get their daughter back. Will pay anyone.

Alfred and Maud Easton

Claudia's parents, held at the Garrison.

Description: Butler and lady's maid to the Ridgelys.

Mannerisms: Polite to their jailers out of habit.

Intent: Protect Claudia. They know where she hid first: the Sheets.

Hamilton Frederick, PI

Private investigator, North Harbor.

Description: A rumpled coat, a bad knee, a wall of newsprint.

Mannerisms: Answers questions with prices.

Intent: Finish the job he was paid for. Knows the Rue Blanc address.

Hazel Attwater

Underground journalist, The Worker.

Description: Ink to the elbows, a printer's apron.

Mannerisms: Asks who sent you before anything else.

Intent: Print the truth about Paschendale. Holds the leaked report.

Widow Ashe

Fortune teller, East Row.

Description: Black lace, rings on every finger, a cold parlour.

Mannerisms: Lowers her voice when the lamps flicker.

Intent: Earn the Ridgelys' fee without being found by what blocks her.

Professor Magrat

Natural philosophy, Meskawaki University. Held.

Description: Brilliant, vain, frightened.

Mannerisms: Lectures his jailers.

Intent: Survive. He helped the Special Police once, and says so only if cornered.

Aubrey Salisbury

Assistant Coroner, The Repose.

Description: A records man, ink not blood on his cuffs.

Mannerisms: Quotes file numbers.

Intent: Have his inquests back. Shows the party the records to spite the Special Police.

Sergeant Cecil Frost

Desk sergeant, Special Police Garrison.

Description: Prim, pressed, and always behind the ledger.

Mannerisms: Cites the regulation number.

Intent: Keep the ledger closed and the party out.

Sergeant Henry Sharpe

Union Station Watch House.

Description: A tired Watch sergeant with a borrowed wagon he wishes he had not lent.

Mannerisms: Looks at the door when Standard is named.

Intent: Stay out of the Special Police's business.

Bette Huerlock

Washerwoman, the Sheets.

Description: Red arms, a sharp eye.

Mannerisms: Talks while she works.

Intent: Feed her children. Saw the raid.

Cissy Gelena

Flower-seller, East Row.

Description: A young girl with a cart outside the perfume shop.

Mannerisms: Warm, quick, nosy.

Intent: Help Claudia, who was kind to her.

Evelyn Ridgely

Law student, Magrat's assistant.

Description: Torn sleeves, a bruised wrist, chained in the safehouse.

Mannerisms: Clear and angry once free.

Intent: Find Claudia. Heard where Standard took her.

pages.name: The Special Police and the Smiling Man
pages.html:
Special Police Captain

Medium humanoid, CR 7.

AC13; HP54; three attacks: Service Revolver+11/2d6+4; Baton Strike+11/1d10+4; Sweep the Line DC15/5d6+5

Description: An officer of the Special Police with a ruined night's sleep and a revolver drawn.

Mannerisms: Barks Orders: allies have advantage on the first attack against one target. Cover Fire ends a hostile's movement. Rank: allies within 30 ft. add +2 to attacks.

Intent: Hold the flat. Keep the doctor alive.

Traits. Special Training: advantage against a creature that has not yet acted this round. Burst Fire: a 10-ft. cube within 80 ft., DC 15 Dex or 2d8 piercing.

Special Guard

Medium humanoid, CR 5. The Elite Special Police.

AC11; HP21; two attacks: Service Revolver+7/2d6+4; Baton Strike+7/1d8+3; Steady Aim+8/3d6+2

Description: Good plain coats, no badges, the best shots in the Special Police.

Mannerisms: Duck Behind Cover as a bonus action. Return Fire when an ally is shot.

Intent: Take the target, leave no witness.

Hungry Crowd

Gargantuan swarm of Medium humanoids, CR 10.

AC18; HP180; two attacks: Piling On+5/2d4+4; Rip and Drag DC16/4d6+4

Description: The poor of the Sheets, hundreds strong and done being raided.

Mannerisms: Take What We Want, DC 14 Dex or lose an item. Gives Ground 15 ft. when hit in melee. At half HP, a DC 12 Wisdom save or it scatters.

Intent: Drive out anyone who looks like police.

Uniformed Constable

Medium humanoid, CR 1. The Watch.

Overview
pages.html:
No Shadow Anywhere

The Clarion Society holds Dr. Aldous Pemberton in a small white room ringed by lamps, so he casts no shadow. His shadow is the Smiling Man, and it can leave him only while he sleeps. The party questions the doctor and the people around him: Evelyn Ridgely, Sergeant Bay, President Byrgenwright, and Hazel Attwater of The Worker. Every answer points to the Lord of Light's ball. Then Bryony Thatch finds a way to end the Smiling Man: a ritual from the Pale Journal pages that splits the light in a man from the dark. For it to work, Pemberton has to sleep.

Episode Summary
Players 3–6, Level 11
Duration ~4 hours
Pacing Interrogation; Investigation; Ritual Combat
Scenes 4
Cast Dr. Pemberton; President Byrgenwright; Bryony Thatch; Evelyn Ridgely; Sergeant Bay; Hazel Attwater; the Smiling Man
Reward A reason to attend the ball; the end of the Smiling Man
References Doom Counter; Dread Insight; Pale Journal pages; ritual chamber map; Smiling Man stat block

Timeline

Fifteen years ago. A collector had the Pale Journals stolen from the Temple of Anhur in Sai Abbadon.

Six months ago. The Special Police began building super-soldiers from a serum found in one of the Journals.

Weeks ago. At Paschendale the serum turned the volunteers into monsters. The city was told it was a victory.

Days ago. The players saved Freitman Bay, freed Evelyn Ridgely, and captured Dr. Pemberton. Colonel Standard took Bay's wife, Claudia, to the Clairvoyant.

Last night. The Clarion Society shut Pemberton in a white room under the lamps. The players have kept him awake since.

Today. The Worker is passing from hand to hand. Pemberton is very tired.

Episode Structure

Almost all of this episode takes place in the Clarion Society clubhouse. There is no trail to follow; the players gather answers from the people in the building and from Hazel Attwater at The Worker's press.

Four sources each hold one piece. Together they put Colonel Standard and the Clairvoyant at the Lord of Light's ball. That is the reason to go, and getting in is Episode Eight's problem.

The episode ends with the ritual. Bryony Thatch and President Byrgenwright cast it; the players feed the circle and fight the Smiling Man through a rift into the Shadowfell.

pages.name: The Doom Counter
pages.html:
Start: equal to the party's number of Dread Insights.

Add 1 Doom for every hour of play Pemberton is kept awake, and every time a player tests the lamps or the straps.

Escalating Doom

Mark Escalation
3 Pemberton nods. Keeping him awake takes a DC 12 check each scene.
6 He begs to sleep. DC 15.
9 He drifts mid-sentence. DC 18.
12 He cannot be kept awake. The ritual must begin now.

Manifesting Doom

Cost Doom
1 Mythos Disadvantage
1 Murphy's Law
2 A Shadow on the Wall
2 The Wrong Fragment
5 Activate one Dread Ability

pages.name: Scene 1: The White Room
pages.html:
The Clarion Society, Ash Ward. Day. ~60 min

A small room painted white from floor to ceiling. Brass lamps on iron stands ring a wooden chair in the middle. The man strapped into it casts no shadow.

What's Happening. Dr. Pemberton sits in the chair, awake and exhausted. A Clarion Society member keeps watch at the door. Evelyn Ridgely and Sergeant Freitman Bay are in the clubhouse. President Byrgenwright wanders from room to room and can turn up anywhere, this room included.

The Worker. If the players did not pick up The Worker in Episode Six ("The Clairvoyant Behind the Experiments," Episode Six handouts), it is in the clubhouse today. Hand it out. Its byline, Hazel Attwater, is the lead out of the building.

Clues. Each source knows one thing. See Who Knows What.

Skill Checks

Insight DC 14. Pemberton is telling the truth: he does not know where Standard reports or how he travels.

Medicine DC 12. Pemberton has not slept in more than a day. He will not last another.

Investigation DC 10. The lamps leave no shadow anywhere in the room, not even under the chair.

Who Knows What

Source Gives the Players
Pemberton Standard works for someone.
Evelyn Standard is picking up his dress uniform for the ball.
Byrgenwright Someone high in the government has been secretly tracking the Pale Journal page.
Hazel Attwater Her source thinks the Clairvoyant will be at the ball.

Sergeant Bay. He does not know that Standard left the safehouse with Claudia. Telling him is the players' choice.

President Byrgenwright. He gives his piece in fragments and non sequiturs: a ministry stamp, a name crossed out on a library slip, "they asked after the page twice." Let the players put it together. Do not explain it for them.

Doom

Mythos Disadvantage. Disadvantage on one roll.

Murphy's Law. A strap gives, a lamp needs trimming, a door sticks.

A Shadow on the Wall. For one moment someone sees a grin in a corner where no shadow should be. Wisdom save or Frightened until the end of the scene.

The Wrong Fragment. Byrgenwright says something true about a different matter, and a player believes it is about this one.

Activate one Dread Ability. Trigger a Dread Insight already held by a player.

pages.name: Scene 2: Hazel Attwater
pages.html:
The Worker's press, Meskawaki University. Day. ~30 min

What's Happening. Hazel prints The Worker in a cellar under the university (Foundry 06.14). She trusts no one sent by money or by the state.

Clues. Her source thinks the Clairvoyant will be at the ball. She will not say who the source is.

Skill Checks

Persuasion DC 15. Hazel tells what her source said. On a failure, she wants something first: a story she can print.

Insight DC 14. She is protecting the source, not lying.

Scene Flow. When the players have the pieces, or the Counter reaches 12, run Scene 3.

pages.name: Scene 3: Building the Ritual
pages.html:
The Clarion Society. ~30 min

What's Happening. Bryony Thatch has been reading the Pale Journal pages the party has found. She asks one player to work through them with her. Together they put together a ritual that separates the light and dark parts of a person so the soul can be healed. Bryony cannot cast it alone. She asks President Byrgenwright to cast it with her.

The Price. The ritual needs Pemberton asleep. The players must let him sleep, in the ritual room, inside the circle.

Skill Checks

Arcana DC 16. The player and Bryony read the ritual right. On a failure, it still works, but the first blast in Scene 4 does nothing.

Persuasion DC 12. Byrgenwright agrees. He drifts off the subject twice before he does.

pages.name: The Ritual Chamber
pages.html:
Reading the Map

The ritual room is a white stone chamber in the Clarion Society. When the ritual begins, its back wall opens onto the Shadowfell, a broken land of rock and chasm that runs off the edge of the map. Map: 07.01 Out of the Shadows in Foundry.

1. The altar.

2. Bryony's station.

3. Byrgenwright's station.

4. The circle. Pemberton sleeps at its heart.

5. The circle's points. Four of them: top, bottom, left, right. The players stand here to feed the ritual.

6. The broken wall. The opening into the Shadowfell.

7. The Shadowfell. Where the Smiling Man hides.

pages.name: Scene 4: Out of the Shadows
pages.html:
The ritual room. Night. ~60 min

The circle burns red, gold, and blue on the white floor. Above the sleeping doctor hangs a pale light the size of a man. Behind it, the back wall is gone.

What's Happening. As Pemberton falls asleep, the ritual begins. A floating light, a ghost of the man he was, rises above him. The back wall of the chamber opens onto the Shadowfell. The light speaks: it can feel the shadow hiding in there. Roll initiative.

The Circle. The players stand at the circle's points and feed it. Bryony and Byrgenwright cast from their stations. The ritual protects them both; nothing in the fight can harm them.

The Blasts. On Bryony's turn and on Byrgenwright's turn, the light fires a blast of radiant energy into the Shadowfell. It shows the players where the Smiling Man is, and it weakens him. Choose one effect for each blast.

Blast Effect
Exposed His AC is lowered until his next turn.
Opened Player hits are critical hits until his next turn.
Burned Player hits deal double damage until his next turn.
Dimmed His hits deal half damage until his next turn.
Released End Paralyzed on every player.

The Smiling Man. He fights from the dark. In dim light or darkness, Peel Away makes attacks against him use AC 30. The blasts are what let the players reach him; they are the way to win, not a race to drain 1,080 hit points.

Skill Checks

Perception DC 15. Find the Smiling Man in the Shadowfell without a blast. On a success, the player may attack him this turn.

Scene Flow. When the Smiling Man falls or flees, the rift closes and the light sinks back into the doctor.

pages.name: Resolution
pages.html:
Outcome Ladder.

  • Total success. The Smiling Man falls. Pemberton wakes, and his shadow is only a shadow.
  • Mixed. The Smiling Man escapes with Bag Trick before the rift closes.
  • Total failure. He takes a player's memories with Excise and is gone into the dark.
  • Pyrrhic. He falls, and a player stays Paralyzed in the Shadowfell as it closes.

Rewards. The players leave with a reason to attend the ball: the man who took Claudia and the one he answers to will both be there.

Threads and Dead Ends.

  • The ball. Episode Eight.
  • Claudia. With the Clairvoyant until the child is born.
  • Hazel's source. Unnamed.

pages.html:
Dr. Aldous Pemberton

The smiling doctor. The party's prisoner.

AC11; HP13

Description: Shirtsleeves, round spectacles, red eyes, a smile he cannot stop.

Mannerisms: Begs to sleep. Apologizes for the people his shadow killed.

Intent: Sleep. Knows Standard works for someone, and nothing more.

President Erasmus Byrgenwright

Half-elf. President of the Clarion Society.

AC11; HP13

Description: Very old, very thin, ink on his cuffs and dust on his coat.

Mannerisms: Speaks in fragments. Wanders from room to room.

Intent: Understand what has been let into the city. Casts the ritual with Bryony.

Bryony Thatch

Harengon. Clarion Society recruit.

AC15; HP3

Description: Long ears, ink-stained paws, a stack of journal pages she will not put down.

Mannerisms: Talks fast. Asks three questions for every answer.

Intent: Make the ritual work. Her curiosity runs well ahead of her caution.

Evelyn Ridgely

Law student. Freed from the safehouse.

Description: A bruised wrist and a lawyer's memory for what was said.

Mannerisms: Precise. Angry when she is not believed.

Intent: Find Claudia. Heard that Standard is picking up his dress uniform for the ball.

Sergeant Freitman Bay

The Trooper. Sole survivor of Paschendale.

Description: A soldier the serum changed, keeping very still in a borrowed coat.

Mannerisms: Asks after his wife in every conversation.

Intent: Find Claudia. Does not know Standard has her.

Hazel Attwater

Prints The Worker.

Description: Ink to the elbows, a printer's apron.

Mannerisms: Asks who sent you before anything else.

Intent: Print the truth. Protects her source.
